title: Plotter Improvements For Pattern Printing | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our Avatars in CLO 2025.0 allows you to include all pattern information and customize line styles and displays when printing patterns to a plotter.

Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

summary: ```markdown # Plotter Improvements For Pattern Printing | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe, and we have some great updates with our print layout and exporting to Plotter. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Exporting Patterns to Plotter So, I have my pattern all set up. I've nested it, I've added in seam allowance, and I'm ready to export this out to my Plotter. I even got some annotations in there. There are a few ways to export to a Plotter, and I'm going to go through the two methods we've updated. ### Method 1: Using the Snapshot Icon The first way is to use this little snapshot icon right here. You can select it from inside your print layout, which you can access through your modes. Go to **Print Layout** in the toolbar, and at the bottom, you'll find the snapshot option. 1. **Create a Snapshot**: Select the snapshot icon to create a snapshot of your layout. 2. **Adjust Visibility**: One of the nice updates we've done is allow you to uncheck pattern outlines if you'd like, so that only your seam allowance is displayed. This feature is really helpful because: - You can uncheck various elements such as: - Pattern outlines - Baselines - Internal lines - Graphic lines - Reference lines - You can keep symmetrical instance lines or uncheck that as well. - Choose to show additional information or uncheck it all. 3. **Nesting Header Information**: We have also added nesting header information to the bottom, which you can use along with pattern names and annotations. Once you have made your selections, you can choose your format. I'm going to set it to **1:1** and then save it. ### Method 2: File Export Another way to export is by going to **File** in your top toolbar. Select **Export**, then **Plotter**. A pop-up window will appear. 1. **Customization Options**: Again, we have separated out notches and baselines. Here, you can: - Keep your notches and uncheck baselines. - Uncheck graphic lines or reference lines. - Optionally include pattern outlines, which can be set to dotted or dashed. You won't see these changes in the preview, but you will notice them once you export and save the file. 2. **Size Options**: You have the ability to either shrink to fit or use actual size. For this example, I'm going to choose **shrink to fit** so that everything fits neatly inside my pattern without going outside of it. 3. **Final Adjustments**: I'm going to keep the pattern outlines dotted. After making these selections, I can save the file. ## Review of Exported Information You can see how all of this looks right here. It may appear a little blurry, but you can notice the dashed lines, notches, seam allowance, and all the saved information in your water file. Pretty cool, right? ## Conclusion Thanks so much for watching! If you have any questions, feel free to use the comment section down below. One of our code designers will get back to you. Don't forget to check out all the other great videos we have on our YouTube channel. Thanks again so much for watching, and keep having fun in CLO 2025.0! ```
